That is EXACTLY how I cook prime rib, only way to do it IMHO

I usually sear then finish in oven, what's the benefits of doing it this way? I'm all for it, just interested in what the difference is. Edit: I did watch his youtube, and that 30 min precook takes a lot longer than my total 12 minutes I need to do it the other way. Is it really work the extra 20 minutes?

With a Prime Rib, where you want a long cook time to let it self-marinate in the fat and are aiming for a low finish temp, it means you can get the Exact finished temp you want all the way through and even hold it till the time you want to serve (hours longer if needed) and then finish it right at the end. It's sorta like Sous-vide in that way (with Sous-vide you can have the food "cooking" for 8~10~12 hours and it never gets over-cooked, you just sear the outside at the very end when you're ready to plate/serve).

The benefit is additional control over the finished product. Is it worth it? Once, absolutely so you can see for yourself the difference. Beyond that, only you can decide. For just a simple steak though, I still pan sear (no oven needed).

FWIW, this same method works a treat with cheesecake too (do the cooking on a lower temp to set the cake first, and then brown it at the end), I'll never go back.
